There's a running joke that can never be told too often: every year Apple solemnly declares that year's iPhone Pro to be "the best iPhone we've ever made," as if this were some shocking revelation. But I think there's something of a poignant note about the iPhone 18 Pro, because if the rumours about next year's model are true, this one may well be the final generation of this design language since the iPhone X back in 2017.

Specifically, we expect to see the next significant step towards the "single slab of glass" vision next year, bringing the era of incremental evolution over the past decade to a close…

The evolution of the iPhone Pro

If you line up every generation from the iPhone 12 Pro through to the iPhone 16 Pro, I think most people would struggle to tell them apart at a glance, beyond the move from the notch to the Dynamic Island in 2022. The reason the iPhone 17 Pro stands out is only because of the enlarged camera module and the cosmic orange colourway.

Of course, every generation brings new features, but I think it's fair to say that unless a particular feature holds special appeal for you personally, you really need to skip at least two to three generations before there's a noticeable upgrade experience.

This is absolutely not a criticism of Apple. The reality is that, at the level of conventional form factor design, the smartphone is a mature technology. We don't see huge differences between generations because there's simply very limited room for improvement within the annual framework.

Apple is now experimenting with different form factors, starting with the iPhone Air, and now the iPhone Duo too — and we expect another big leap next year in the form of a 20th anniversary model.

Exactly how Apple will position next year's design remains unclear for now. Initial speculation suggested it would be a standalone model, distinct from the iPhone 19 Pro, but there have also been reports indicating it would be next year's Pro model. There's also the question of whether Apple will use sequential numbering or skip a number to mark the milestone, so it might possibly be called the iPhone 20 Pro.

Personally, I do suspect this will be a new iPhone Pro design, regardless of whether Apple calls it 19 or 20. If so, then the iPhone 18 Pro would be the final iteration of the form factor we've had for six years.

I jumped two generations from the iPhone 16 Pro, so I'll list separately what the yearly models brought me. I'll skip improvements I consider trivial or of no use to me at all, such as the upgrade from a 6-core GPU to a 7-core one and GenLock.

What the iPhone 17 Pro carried over

  • Center Stage front camera, works for both photos and video calls
  • Ultra-stable video
  • Dual-lens simultaneous recording
  • Telephoto lens upgraded from 5x to 8x
  • Telephoto sensor upgraded from 12 megapixels to 48 megapixels
  • ProRes RAW video
  • Better battery life
  • Faster charging speeds

New additions on the iPhone 18 Pro

  • Wider maximum aperture on the main camera
  • Variable aperture on the main camera
  • Pro camera controls (aperture, shutter speed, white balance, histogram)
  • Photographic Styles third generation
  • Smart focus tracking
  • Cinematic mode effects added to standard video
  • Tap-to-zoom and rotate support on the front camera
  • Smaller Dynamic Island, capable of displaying three Live Activities
  • (Even) better battery life
  • (Even) faster charging speeds

My personal… highlights

On a personal basis, during the initial hands-on period, I'll be focusing on five features.

Variable aperture lens

Although the focus is on the variable aperture lens, I've said before that people probably shouldn't set their expectations too high. The maximum aperture is only very marginally wider, and the sensor is so small, so I wouldn't expect to see a huge difference in terms of shallow depth of field.

However, the wider maximum aperture can indeed let in a bit more light, roughly two-thirds of a stop more. How big a difference it makes in practice will only be known after testing, but in theory it should shorten exposure times in Night Mode. Since I use Night Mode a lot, often handheld, I'm really looking forward to giving this feature a try.

Pro camera controls

Being able to control shutter speed will definitely be useful for shots like panning. Having full control over white balance is also bound to be useful. I also expect the histogram will come in handy when manually setting exposure.

When I take photos or edit them on my iPhone, I'm generally not the type who likes adding filters, preferring more traditional adjustments afterwards. So I rarely use the existing Photographic Styles feature, and don't expect to use the latest version much either. But I have to say I'm quite interested in the Film mode, so I'll definitely give that a try.

As for video autofocus, one of the biggest weaknesses is that when the subject is briefly occluded by another object, the lens may shift focus to that occluding object. Smart focus tracking claims to address this issue, so I'll definitely be testing this feature out.

Cinematic mode effects in standard video

I said just a couple of months ago that Apple appears to have forgotten about Cinematic mode video. I said it was a real shame, because if Cinematic mode video were done well, it would absolutely be a game-changer for turning the iPhone into a more serious video camera. Until now, it's been a case of so close, yet so far.

But it seems I was wrong: one of the new features of the iPhone 18 is that Cinematic-style video effects can be applied to footage shot in standard mode.

Now there's no need to decide in advance whether or not to use the mode, which is certainly convenient, but what interests me most is that Apple is paying attention to this feature again. This is a sign that the feature is indeed getting focus, so we can expect it to keep improving in the way Portrait Mode did. I'm really looking forward to testing this feature.

These are the features I think are likely to make the biggest difference for me. What about you? If you've already upgraded to the iPhone 18 Pro, which features convinced you to switch? Feel free to share in the comments.
